Fix a classical model with physical energy measured in joules and a positive inverse-temperature parameter $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$. Its global configuration space is a measurable space $(\mathcal X,\mathscr F)$. For each finite region $\Lambda$, specify a local state measurable space $(\mathcal X_\Lambda,\mathscr F_\Lambda)$, an admissible exterior measurable space $(\mathcal E_\Lambda,\mathscr E_\Lambda)$, a measurable exterior restriction map $r_\Lambda:(\mathcal X,\mathscr F)\to(\mathcal E_\Lambda,\mathscr E_\Lambda)$, and a measurable concatenation map $c_\Lambda:\mathcal X_\Lambda\times\mathcal E_\Lambda\to\mathcal X$. Require $r_\Lambda(c_\Lambda(x,\eta))=\eta$ for every $x\in\mathcal X_\Lambda$ and $\eta\in\mathcal E_\Lambda$, and write $x\eta:=c_\Lambda(x,\eta)$. Specify a jointly measurable conditional energy $H_\Lambda:\mathcal X_\Lambda\times\mathcal E_\Lambda\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $+\infty$ marks a forbidden local state, and a measurable kernel $\eta\mapsto m_\Lambda^\eta$ of positive $\sigma$-finite reference measures on $(\mathcal X_\Lambda,\mathscr F_\Lambda)$; $\sigma$-finite means that $\mathcal X_\Lambda$ is a countable union of measurable sets of finite $m_\Lambda^\eta$-measure. The reference normalization and any units carried by its coordinates are part of the model data. For a thermodynamic partition function, choose the reference normalization so $Z_\Lambda^\eta$ is dimensionless. The product $\beta H_\Lambda$ is dimensionless.

For $\eta\in\mathcal E_\Lambda$, define
$$Z_\Lambda^\eta:=\int_{\mathcal X_\Lambda}e^{-\beta H_\Lambda(x\mid\eta)}\,dm_\Lambda^\eta(x),\qquad \gamma_\Lambda(C\mid\eta):=(Z_\Lambda^\eta)^{-1}\int_{\mathcal X_\Lambda}\mathbf1_C(x\eta)e^{-\beta H_\Lambda(x\mid\eta)}\,dm_\Lambda^\eta(x),\quad C\in\mathscr F,$$
with $e^{-\beta(+\infty)}:=0$. Adopt these conditional probability kernels only when $0<Z_\Lambda^\eta<\infty$ for every finite $\Lambda$ and admissible $\eta$, and when their dependence on $\eta$ is measurable. A probability measure $\mu$ on $(\mathcal X,\mathscr F)$ is a DLR state for this adopted model if, for every finite $\Lambda$ and every $C\in\mathscr F$,
$$\mu(C)=\int_{\mathcal X}\gamma_\Lambda(C\mid r_\Lambda(y))\,d\mu(y).$$
A specification is a family of these probability kernels that is **proper** when $\gamma_\Lambda(r_\Lambda^{-1}(D)\mid\eta)=\mathbf1_D(\eta)$ for every $D\in\mathscr E_\Lambda$ and $\eta\in\mathcal E_\Lambda$, and **consistent** when $\gamma_\Lambda\gamma_\Delta f=\gamma_\Lambda f$ for every bounded measurable $f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R$ and finite $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda$. Here $\gamma_\Lambda(f\mid\eta):=\int_{\mathcal X}f(y)\,\gamma_\Lambda(dy\mid\eta)$, and composition is explicitly $(\gamma_\Lambda\gamma_\Delta f)(\eta):=\int_{\mathcal X}\gamma_\Delta(f\mid r_\Delta(y))\,\gamma_\Lambda(dy\mid\eta)$. These identities are required when a DLR specification is asserted; normalization alone does not imply them.

In the finite-alphabet lattice instance, let $A$ be finite and nonempty, $\mathcal X=A^{\mathbb Z^d}$ with the cylinder-generated Borel $\sigma$-algebra, $\mathcal X_\Lambda=A^\Lambda$ with its power-set $\sigma$-algebra, and $\mathcal E_\Lambda=A^{\Lambda^c}$. The restriction map is $r_\Lambda(\sigma)=\sigma|_{\Lambda^c}$ and concatenation is coordinatewise patching. For the finite-range interaction of [[def-csm-finite-range-lattice-interaction]], use counting measure on $A^\Lambda$ and the energy $E_\Lambda(\cdot\mid\eta)$ in joules; the resulting kernels are exactly those in [[def-csm-lattice-gibbs-specification]]. The consistency result [[lem-csm-lattice-specification-consistency]] supplies their properness and consistency. The cylinder-measure extension in [[lem-csm-lattice-product-and-measure-compactness]] uses the Countable Choice axiom [[def-countable-choice]] to construct an infinite-volume probability; no finite conditional sum spends that choice assumption.

When particle-number sectors are present, use the exact interface of [[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]]. For species counts $N_a$ with total $N=\sum_aN_a\ge1$ in $d$ spatial dimensions, the phase-space definition [[def-csm-phase-space-reference]] sets the labelled reference to $m_N=c_N\Lambda_N$ with arbitrary $c_N>0$. This postulate chooses $c_N=a_0^{-dN}$, where $a_0>0$ is a prescribed reference action in joule-seconds, and uses the species factor $1/\prod_aN_a!$ in the normalized quotient reference. Equivalently, the symmetric labelled integral uses $(\prod_aN_a!\,a_0^{dN})^{-1}dq\,dp$; the factorial is included once, and the phase-volume dimension $(\mathrm{J\,s})^{dN}$ makes this reference dimensionless. For the vacuum sector $N=0$, define the zero-fold phase space to be a singleton with unit Dirac reference measure (consistent with $0!=1$ and $a_0^0=1$); in a finite region with nonempty exterior, the local vacuum still has the energy $H_\Lambda(\varnothing\mid\eta)$ in its Gibbs weight. If the thermal-wavelength convention of [[def-csm-gibbs-physical-parameters]] is used, set $h_{\rm ref}=a_0$; omit the species factorial for operationally distinguishable labels. These are adopted reference and counting conventions, not consequences of Hamiltonian mechanics or evidence of equilibration. No empirical parameter, measured transition temperature, or uncertainty is asserted here.

This is a model postulate. Normalization, stationarity of a Hamiltonian flow, and finite-volume calculations do not prove equilibration or establish that the model describes nature.

For a declared classical model with $N_a$ operationally indistinguishable
particles of each species $a$, label those particles by
$\{(a,i):1\le i\le N_a\}$ on the auxiliary labelled cover, and let
$S_{N_a}$ denote the permutation group of that species' finite label set.
The product group $G=\prod_a S_{N_a}$ acts on the labelled phase space
$\Gamma_N=T^*Q_N$ by the cotangent lifts of within-species permutations. Let
$\Pi_N:\Gamma_N\to\Gamma_N/G$ be its measurable orbit map from
[[def-csm-phase-space-reference]]. Choose $a_0>0$ as a fixed primitive
reference parameter with action units J s; [[def-cm01-units]] supplies its
dimension, not its value or the choice of this parameter. Here $d$ is the
number of spatial dimensions and $N=\sum_aN_a$. No numerical value or
identification of $a_0$ with Planck's constant is imposed.

Use the weighted labelled lift
$$m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}:=\frac{1}{\prod_aN_a!\,a_0^{dN}}\,d\Lambda_N =\frac{1}{\prod_aN_a!\,a_0^{dN}}\,dq\,dp$$
on $\Gamma_N$, where $d\Lambda_N$ is the Liouville density and the last
expression is its coordinate density in canonical charts, with coordinates
read in SI numerical units. The coordinate volume $dq\,dp$ has action
dimension $(\mathrm{J\,s})^{dN}$, so the reference is dimensionless. The
physical quotient reference is
$$\bar m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}(B):=m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}(\Pi_N^{-1}(B))\qquad(B\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{quot}}).$$
Thus $m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$ is on the labelled cover $\Gamma_N$, and
$\bar m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}=(\Pi_N)_*m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$ is on
$\Gamma_N/G$; with $c_N=a_0^{-dN}$, the latter is exactly the normalized
quotient reference of [[def-csm-phase-space-reference]].

Physical observables for indistinguishable particles are measurable
$G$-invariant functions $A:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R$, equivalently measurable
functions $\bar A$ on the quotient with $A=\bar A\circ\Pi_N$. For every such
observable with an integrable expectation, its integral against
$m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$ equals the quotient integral against
$\bar m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$. A labelled density represents a physical state on
the quotient only if it is invariant under $G$ almost everywhere with respect
to $m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$; an invariant representative may then be used. In
particular, an indistinguishable-particle Hamiltonian must be invariant under
these permutations (or agree almost everywhere with its permuted versions
when only its Gibbs density is at issue). A label-specific coordinate
statistic on the lift is not itself a quotient observable. Under a
permutation-invariant state its marginal law
can instead be interpreted as the law of a uniformly selected particle within
the same species, or of a uniformly selected coordinate of the same type
within that species. Symmetric sums and averages within each species are
quotient observables.
Calculations of labelled momentum components in
[[pthm-csm-canonical-momentum-equipartition]] use this symmetric labelled
lift, and their permutation-invariant kinetic sums and averages are physical
observables.

If labels are operationally distinguishable, omit the corresponding
permutation factor and use the labelled phase space directly. The convention
is part of the preparation and reference model; it is not deduced from
Hamiltonian mechanics. Whether a quantity is represented by a gauge-dependent
canonical momentum or by a gauge-invariant mechanical momentum is fixed by the
stated model and gauge convention. No quantum exchange law, actual preparation
mechanism, or empirical indistinguishability test is asserted.

Use SI units. Let $k_B>0$ be Boltzmann's constant in joules per kelvin, let $T>0$ be absolute temperature in kelvin, and define $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in joules$^{-1}$. For a finite-alphabet lattice model in dimension $d\geq1$, the lattice spacing $a>0$ is in metres; a spin is a dimensionless label. In the nearest-neighbor Ising convention
$$H_\Lambda=-J_{\rm I}\sum_{\{i,j\}\subset\Lambda,\ |i-j|_1=1}s_i s_j-h\sum_{i\in\Lambda}s_i,$$
the coupling $J_{\rm I}$ and field parameter $h$ are energies in joules, so $\beta J_{\rm I}$ and $\beta h$ are dimensionless. Here $h$ is an energy bias per spin, not by itself a magnetic-field strength.

For a finite nonempty region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$, set $H_\Lambda:=H^{\mathrm{free}}_\Lambda$ from [[def-csm-finite-range-lattice-interaction]], with each physical interaction value $\Phi_r$ and total energy measured in joules. Thus the partition below uses free boundary conditions: only interaction supports contained in $\Lambda$ contribute. Exterior-conditioned energies $E_\Lambda(\cdot\mid\eta)$ and their partitions carry a separate exterior label and are not denoted by this $H_\Lambda$ or $Z_\Lambda$. Let $Z_\Lambda=\sum_{\sigma\in A^\Lambda}e^{-\beta H_\Lambda(\sigma)}$ and define dimensionless pressure per site $p_\Lambda=|\Lambda|^{-1}\log Z_\Lambda$. When $p=\lim_{n\to\infty}|B_n|^{-1}\log Z_{B_n}$ exists for cubes $B_n=[-n,n]^d\cap\mathbb Z^d$, define physical pressure $\mathsf P=k_BT\,p/a^d$ in J m$^{-d}$ (pascals when $d=3$). For a stationary state $\mu$ on a finite alphabet (a probability invariant under every translation $(\theta_j\sigma)_x=\sigma_{x+j}$), let $H_n=-\sum_{\sigma\in A^{B_n}}\mu_{B_n}(\sigma)\log\mu_{B_n}(\sigma)$ with $0\log0=0$; when the limit exists, its Shannon entropy density is $h_{\rm Sh}=\lim_{n\to\infty}H_n/|B_n|$ in nats per site. The mean energy per site is $u=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}\mathbb E_\mu[\Phi_r]$ in joules per site. Define reference spin entropy density $s=k_Bh_{\rm Sh}/a^d$ and free-energy density $f=u/a^d-Ts$; both are per physical volume. Thus $f$ and $\mathsf P$ have units J m$^{-d}$, while $s$ has units J K$^{-1}$ m$^{-d}$; for $d=3$ these are the usual per-cubic-metre units.

For a continuum model in dimension $d$, let $x,p\in\mathbb R^d$ be position and momentum, let $m_{\rm p}>0$ be particle mass in kilograms, and use kinetic energy $|p|^2/(2m_{\rm p})$. Assume Countable Choice for the Lebesgue change-of-variables interface [[def-countable-choice]]. Tonelli's theorem [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] and the one-dimensional Gaussian integral [[thm-gaussian-integral]] give $\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{-|q|^2}\,d^dq=\pi^{d/2}$. Set $c=\sqrt{\beta/(2m_{\rm p})}>0$ and apply the nonnegative change-of-variables theorem [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]] to the $C^1$ diffeomorphism $q\mapsto cq$ of $\mathbb R^d$ and $f(q)=e^{-|q|^2}$. Since its Jacobian determinant is $c^d$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{-\beta|p|^2/(2m_{\rm p})}\,d^dp=c^{-d}\pi^{d/2}=(2\pi m_{\rm p}k_BT)^{d/2}.$$
Under the phase-space reference measure $d^dx\,d^dp/h_{\rm ref}^d$, with reference action $h_{\rm ref}>0$ in joule-seconds, the integrated momentum factor is
$$h_{\rm ref}^{-d}\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{-\beta|p|^2/(2m_{\rm p})}\,d^dp=\left(\frac{\sqrt{2\pi m_{\rm p}k_BT}}{h_{\rm ref}}\right)^d=\lambda_T^{-d},\qquad \lambda_T=\frac{h_{\rm ref}}{\sqrt{2\pi m_{\rm p}k_BT}}.$$
For chemical potential $\mu$ in joules, define the classical activity $z_c=e^{\beta\mu}\lambda_T^{-d}$, with units $\mathrm m^{-d}$. Thus $\lambda_T$ is a length and $z_c$ is inverse volume. This momentum integration explains the one-particle thermal factor; it does not derive particle indistinguishability or a factorial convention. The choice of $h_{\rm ref}$ is a reference convention, not a consequence of the classical equations of motion. For continuum interactions, the potential hypotheses and energy meaning are as in [[def-csm-stable-superstable-continuum-interaction]].

The parameter status in these formulas is model-relative. $T$, $a$, $J_{\rm I}$, and $h$ are inputs for the chosen lattice model; $m_{\rm p}$ and $\mu$ are inputs for the chosen continuum model. Here $h$ is an energy bias per dimensionless spin, not a magnetic-field strength. The reference action $h_{\rm ref}>0$ is a primitive normalization convention, not a derived quantity or an assertion that it equals Planck's constant. In the current SI, $k_B$ has the exact defining value $1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$; it is a fixed SI conversion constant, not a measured fit parameter in this model. The inverse temperature $\beta$, thermal wavelength $\lambda_T$, activity $z_c$, pressure and entropy densities, energy density $u$, entropy density $s$, and free-energy density $f$ are defined or derived from those inputs and the state as specified above; their formulas do not calibrate the inputs to a material or assert empirical accuracy.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

7. **Uniform tempered exterior boundary.** Under full $\mathrm{AC}$, a superstable regular interaction, a genuine finite-valued positive core with divergent radial integral as in [[lem-tdmath-superquadratic-positive-core]], and fixed $z,\beta>0$, the free-wall grand pressure converges uniformly over the exact square-count exterior class $\Omega(t)$ defined in [[thm-tdmath-uniform-tempered-exterior-pressure]], for each finite $t$. Its limit is the free-cube pressure. This class excludes volume-filling external fields.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$. For $i\in\mathbb Z^d$, let $C_i=i+[0,1)^d$. These are left-closed, right-open cells. For every $x\in\mathbb R^d$, [[lem-integer-part]] supplies the unique integers $i_j$ with $i_j\le x_j<i_j+1$, so $x$ belongs to exactly one $C_i$. The cells are Borel products of closed/open ray intersections and have volume one by [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], whose statement covers this face convention. A finite configuration in $C_i$ is a finite subset of distinct points. Encode it by its cardinality $n\in\mathbb N_0$ and its uniquely lexicographically increasing list of local coordinates $(x_1-i,\ldots,x_n-i)\in([0,1)^d)^n$. Pad the code after its first $n$ coordinates with the zero vector. For fixed $n$, the strictly increasing lists form a Borel subset of $([0,1]^d)^n$, since lexicographic strict order is a finite union of coordinate-equality and coordinate-inequality conditions. Thus all codes form a Borel subset of $\mathbb N_0\times([0,1]^d)^{\mathbb N}$. Each factor $[0,1]^d$ is Polish as a closed subspace of complete $\mathbb R^d$ with a countable dense rational grid; $\mathbb N_0$ with its discrete metric is Polish. The ambient space is Polish by [[cor-countable-products-and-g-delta-subspaces-of-polish-spaces-are-polish]] (and is completely metrized by [[lem-standard-complete-metric-on-a-countable-product]]), so [[lem-borel-subspaces-admit-polish-presentations]] makes the cell space $E_i$ standard Borel. By [[lem-tdmath-counts-generate-configuration-sigma]], its sigma-algebra is generated by the counts $N_B$ for Borel $B\subseteq C_i$.

Use $e^t:=\exp(t)$ for real $t$, with $\exp$ defined by [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]]; for a real measurable function $f$, $e^f$ means the pointwise composition $\exp\circ f$. For $\lambda>0$, give a cell configuration with $n$ points probability $\exp(-\lambda)\lambda^n/n!$ for its count. The probabilities sum to $\exp(-\lambda)\exp(\lambda)=\exp(0)=1$ by the exponential power series and [[thm-exponential-addition-formula]]. Conditional on count $n$, take the $n$-fold product of normalized Lebesgue measure on $C_i$, restrict it to the complement of the collision diagonals, and push it forward by lexicographic sorting. The product exists by the finite product-measure theorem; each collision diagonal is null by Tonelli and the fact that Lebesgue measure gives every singleton measure zero, so the restricted measure still has mass one. Sorting is Borel on the finitely many permutation regions of the no-collision set. This defines a law $\pi_{i,\lambda}$ on $E_i$; for $n=0$, use the empty product and the empty configuration. Let $\Omega=\prod_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}E_i$ with its product cylinder sigma-algebra. The product sigma-algebra is generated by the cell-coordinate sigma-algebras, each generated by counts on Borel subsets of its bounded cell by [[lem-tdmath-counts-generate-configuration-sigma]]. Conversely every bounded-region count is a finite sum of these cell counts, since a bounded set meets finitely many cells. Thus the product cylinder sigma-algebra is exactly the sigma-algebra generated by all bounded-Borel count maps. For each $\lambda>0$, $Q_\lambda$ denotes the unique probability on $\Omega$ whose finite cell marginals are the products of the corresponding $\pi_{i,\lambda}$. Existence and uniqueness follow from [[thm-kolmogorov-extension-for-standard-borel-coordinate-spaces]]. In particular every translation $T_x$ is measurable since $N_A(T_x\omega)=N_{A-x}(\omega)$. The unit-intensity reference is $Q:=Q_1$.

Identify each $\omega\in\Omega$ with the simple locally finite counting measure obtained by uniting its finite cell configurations. For a bounded Borel set $A\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, write $N_A(\omega)=\omega(A)$ and $|A|$ for its Lebesgue measure. Define translation by $T_x\omega(A)=\omega(A-x)$ for $x\in\mathbb R^d$. The next item proves that under $Q_\lambda$, counts in disjoint bounded Borel sets are independent Poisson random variables with means $\lambda|A|$ and that $Q_\lambda$ is translation invariant. This item is a mathematical reference construction and makes no physical claim.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix $d\geq1$. For every bounded Borel set $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ and $n\in\mathbb N_0$, the unit-intensity Poisson law restricted to $N_D=n$, represented on ordered simple tuples in $D^n$ before forgetting labels, is the pushforward of $e^{-|D|}/n!$ times product Lebesgue measure. Now fix a nonempty bounded Borel region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$, a stable even Borel pair potential $\phi$ with finite range $R>0$ as in [[def-csm-continuum-dlr-kernels]], a locally finite exterior configuration $\eta\subset\Lambda^c$, and $z,\beta>0$. Let $m=N_{\Lambda^R}(\eta)$, with $\Lambda^R=\{y:\operatorname{dist}_2(y,\Lambda)\leq R\}$. Then the partition integral in [[def-csm-continuum-dlr-kernels]] obeys
$$e^{-|\Lambda|}\leq Z_\Lambda^\eta(z,\beta)\leq e^{-|\Lambda|}\exp\!\left(z|\Lambda|e^{\beta B(1+2m)}\right)<\infty.$$
Consequently $\gamma_\Lambda^\eta$ is a Borel probability kernel in $\eta$. For every nonempty bounded Borel region $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda$, the extended kernels satisfy $\gamma_\Lambda\gamma_\Delta=\gamma_\Lambda$, and their fixed measures are exactly the probability laws whose conditional distribution inside each $\Lambda$, given the exterior, is $\gamma_\Lambda^\eta$.

Assume AC, fix $d\geq1$ and $\lambda>0$, and let $Q_\lambda$ be the configuration law of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. Define the intensity measure on Borel sets by $\Lambda_{Q_\lambda}(A):=E_{Q_\lambda}N_A$, where $N_A=\omega(A)$ and the nonnegative expectation may be infinite. For pairwise disjoint bounded Borel sets $A_1,\ldots,A_r\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, the restrictions $\omega|_{A_1},\ldots,\omega|_{A_r}$ are independent, each count $N_{A_j}$ has Poisson law with mean $\lambda|A_j|$, and the joint law of counts on any finite disjoint family is the product of those Poisson laws. In particular, $Q_\lambda$ is invariant under every translation $T_x$, and $\Lambda_{Q_\lambda}(A)=\lambda|A|$ for every Borel $A$. For every bounded Borel $A$ and real $a$, its count also has the exact exponential moment
$$E_{Q_\lambda}e^{aN_A}=\exp\!\left(\lambda|A|(e^a-1)\right).$$

For $x\in\mathbb R$, define
$$\exp(x):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{\iota(n!)}, \qquad e:=\exp(1),$$
provided by the all-real convergence proved in [[lem-exponential-series-has-infinite-radius]]. Here $n!\in\mathbb N$ is the factorial of [[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]], $\iota(n!)$ is its nonzero real image ([[def-canonical-natural]], [[lem-of-naturals-positive]]), and powers and series are those of [[def-integer-power]] and [[def-series]].

This is a real power series centred at $0$ ([[def-real-power-series-and-radius-of-convergence]]). No logarithm, irrational power, or differential equation enters the definition.

For all real $x,y$,
$$\exp(x+y)=\exp(x)\exp(y).$$
The exponential function is continuous and strictly increasing on $\mathbb R$.

For $x>0$, define $\log x$ to be the unique real $y$ such that $\exp(y)=x$. This is well-defined because [[cor-exponential-is-a-bijection-onto-positive-reals]] states that $\exp:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)$ is a bijection.

Thus $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is the inverse function of $\exp$. In particular, $\log(\exp y)=y$ for every $y\in\mathbb R$ and $\exp(\log x)=x$ for every $x>0$.

derivations.claim:
Under [A3], an $N$-particle configuration has numerical positional energy $H_N^c=cN$. Its unit-Poisson normalized grand partition is
$$Z_{Q,L}^c=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}\!\left[e^{\alpha N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta cN_{\Lambda_L}}\right] =E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}e^{(\alpha-\beta c)N_{\Lambda_L}} =\exp\!\left(L^3(e^{\alpha-\beta c}-1)\right)$$
by [F4] and the exponential addition law [F5].

By [F3], the $N$-point sector of $Q_{\Lambda_L}$ contributes $e^{-L^3}/N!$ times the positional integral in [A3]. Summing sectors therefore gives $Z_{Q,L}^c=e^{-L^3}\Xi_L^c$, so [A3] yields $\Xi_L^c=\exp(L^3e^{\alpha-\beta c})$.
